label: fs-integration-by-parts-needs-no-integrability-hypothesis

VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: The counterexample uses the concrete interval [0,1] (a<b) with u=G and v(x)=x. The left side ∫_0^1 G exists because G is differentiable hence continuous, and continuous on a closed interval implies integrable (thm-continuous-implies-integrable). The right side contains ∫_0^1 u'v = ∫_0^1 x G'(x). The function x G'(x) is unbounded (step 3.1), so by the library’s definitions (def-darboux-sums, def-darboux-integral) it has no Darboux sums and the integral symbol does not denote. Endpoints are handled correctly: differentiability on [0,1] is defined via one-sided limits at the endpoints (def-derivative). No degenerate/empty cases affect the argument.

SOURCES: All 19 supplied items were inspected: cex-a-function-with-a-primitive-that-is-not-integrable, cor-differentiable-implies-continuous, def-bounded-set, def-canonical-natural, def-complete-ordered-field, def-continuity-real, def-darboux-integral, def-darboux-sums, def-derivative, def-integer-power, def-interval, def-ordered-field, lem-derivative-of-a-power, lem-of-naturals-positive, thm-algebra-of-derivatives, thm-continuous-implies-integrable, thm-ftc-second-part, thm-integration-by-parts, thm-of-archimedean. Every citation in the refutation aligns with the quoted content of the dependency; for instance, def-darboux-sums explicitly requires boundedness, and thm-of-archimedean justifies the cofinality claim.

CHECKED: Title “FALSE: if u and v are differentiable on [a,b] then …”, public statement [A1], and all six numbered steps (1.1–5.1) together with the Remarks. Each step is logically valid and correctly uses the cited facts. The witness G is differentiable (cex item), v(x)=x is differentiable, the left integral exists, and the right integral is undefined because the integrand is unbounded; therefore the claimed identity is not a true statement—a valid refutation of the false claim.
